An umbrella term for various innate physical conditions in which chromosomes, gonads, hormones, or body structure do not completely fit typical definitions of male or female. In medicine, it is also called "disorders of sex development (DSD)" or "variations in physical sex development." It concerns physical traits and is a separate axis from gender identity and sexual orientation. It does not mean a "third sex," nor does it force people into a specific gender; gender identity varies by person (male, female, non-binary, etc., and some are transgender). While it is a separate concept from transgender, the two can overlap, and it is considered part of LGBTQIA+.
